Tab-indented source mixed with fixed-format conventions. Author note 'VAN TZE SHAN' and date '5/8/19' suggest a Southeast Asian shop (possibly Singapore/Malaysia).
evidence: PROCEDURE DIVISION USING LINK-TYPE, LINK-DDMMYYYY, LINK-ERROR-CODE

purpose.domain_detail: Date validation subprogram supporting both DDMMYYYY and YYYYMMDD formats
purpose.summary: A called subprogram (F-CKDATE) that validates a date passed via linkage. It accepts a type indicator ('D' for DDMMYYYY or 'Y' for YYYYMMDD) and an 8-digit date, checks month validity, day range (using a packed days-per-month table), and leap year, returning an error code of 100020 if invalid.

notable_features: LINKAGE SECTION with PROCEDURE DIVISION USING
EVALUATE for dispatch on date format type
REDEFINES with OCCURS for days-per-month table
88-level condition names for leap year and valid month
Leap year check via DIVIDE remainder into same field (destructive)
verdict.notes: Source uses tab characters for indentation mixed with fixed-format column conventions, causing some lines to exceed column 72 (4 long lines noted). The leap year check is a simplified modulo-4 only (no century correction). The DIVIDE overwrites WS-YYYY with the remainder, which is intentional but unusual. Overall structure is consistent with a small production utility subprogram.
